notes_list.title: Phenol Tests and Reactions
notes_list.basic_overview: Phenols show characteristic acidity and color/complexation reactions because the phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilized.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Ferric chloride can give colored complexes with many phenols; bromination of activated phenols is rapid; phenol reacts with base to form phenoxide more readily than ordinary alcohols.
notes_list.examples: Phenol + Br2(aq) gives polybromination under suitable conditions. FeCl3 is a common qualitative test but not universal for every phenolic compound.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Aqueous/basic medium favors phenoxide; bromination conditions determine degree of substitution.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Phenoxide formation increases ring activation. Electrophilic substitution occurs readily at ortho/para positions because the OH group donates by resonance.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Acid-base equilibrium is rapid compared with many downstream substitutions; resonance stabilization controls acidity.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Use tests as a combined identification scheme, not isolated proof.
notes_list.common_traps: Not every FeCl3-positive compound is a simple phenol; hydroxamic acids and other chelating species can also respond.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
